newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Western Cape, Free State, Gauteng, Northern Cape and Mpumalanga had spent well over 60 percent of their housing allocations by September, a marked improvement against last year that reduces the prospect of significant rollovers next year.

- Proposed policy guidelines which stipulated that the successful applicant for the Cape Town metropolitan casino licence would have to contribute more than 100 million rand to a community facility would be presented to the Western Cape cabinet, sources said.

- Electrical and electronics group Reunert Ltd lifted attributable income after abnormal items seven percent to 203 million rand in the year to September after tough trading conditions were exacerbated by the slow delivery of South African telecommunications structure.
- The capital and equity markets bounced back as investors picked up bargains after Monday's gloom-driven slide, while the rand regained some composure.
- The Johannesburg Stock Exchange's all-share index ended firmer after a roller-coaster day on the financial markets.
- The Premier group on Tuesday fired Chris Niehaus, managing director of electronics group Teltron for ten years, after a disciplinary hearing into irregular activities.
- Barlow Ltd and Defy, two of the largest appliance manufacturers, are discussing strategic takeover options but no announcements are in the offing, directors said.
- About 200 charred bodies, many of them still burning, were seen at the crash site south-west of New Delhi after a Saudi Arabian Boeing 747 and a Kazakh Tupelov 154 collided in mid-air on Tuesday.
